answerable: Runoff generation (surface + subsurface runoff) at the two in-domain columns spanning the mid-to-high Naches elevation gradient
Relative roles of elevation/snowpack and soil texture as runoff drivers via cross-column comparison
Evaluation of simulated total runoff against USGS stream gauge data within HUC 17030002 (1980-2018 forcing)
not_answerable: Column at (46.62, -119.90) lies ~0.6 deg east of the Naches bbox eastern edge (-120.5) and is outside HUC 17030002; runoff there is not representative of the Naches domain
Full basin-integrated streamflow routing (single-column ELM produces per-column runoff, not routed hydrographs)

parsed.n_justification: User selected three points. Two (46.85,-121.05 and 47.02,-120.88) fall inside the Naches bbox and capture a mid/high elevation gradient ideal for snow-driven runoff. The third (46.62,-119.90) is outside the domain, so it was relocated to a valid low-elevation Naches location (46.55,-120.55) near the outlet to retain a three-point elevation transect for runoff-generation contrast.
assumptions: STOP_N=39 with STOP_OPTION=nyears runs the full 1980-2018 forcing period; precede with an accelerated/spin-up cycle to equilibrate soil moisture and snow states before analysis.

The out-of-domain point (46.62,-119.90) was relocated to (46.55,-120.55) inside HUC 17030002 near the basin outlet; if the original coordinate is required it should be treated as a separate non-Naches control.
Soil textures are assigned from typical Naches gradient (coarser/rockier at higher elevation) and should be overridden with SSURGO/gridded surface dataset values where available.
Single-column ELM yields point runoff fluxes; comparison to USGS gauges is at the runoff-generation (mm/day) level, not routed discharge.
Monthly and daily history output (hist_mfilt/hist_nhtfrq) should be set to capture snowmelt-driven runoff timing; daily resolution recommended for QRUNOFF/QSNOMELT.
